name: Kelly No Brakes
bio: Open the day in the intimate Folklore Rooms. Kelly No Brakes’ 2026 releases include “Kelly” and “I Wish To Be Loved By You”. A chance to get acquainted with a new name before the day gets loud.

name: Really Good Time
bio: Dublin’s Really Good Time bring noisy guitars, big hooks and an adventurous streak. Matching jumpsuits are a visual signature; the music draws together the punch of rock with a danceable, playful impulse.
listen: Escape From the Mountain of Spit
actualNote: Only one song — then we had to evacuate Green Door Store because of a leak in the roof.

name: MLEKO
bio: A seven-piece from Manchester making restless, unpredictable music they call “Gub Rock”. Brass, tension and sudden changes of direction meet a playful sensibility. Their debut EP is The Feast of St. Perpetua.

name: SNAYX
bio: A Brighton punk trio built around distorted bass, sharp hooks and explosive live energy. Expect a forceful change of pace as the route reaches the seafront: compact, direct and made for a moving crowd.

name: Plantoid
bio: A Brighton band stretching psychedelic rock through jazz, heavy riffs and intricate rhythmic changes. Ethereal vocals move above a dense, exploratory instrumental sound. Stay at Chalk after SNAYX for a very different kind of intensity.

name: Iguana Death Cult
bio: Rotterdam’s Iguana Death Cult combine garage-rock bite with a restless psychedelic edge. Their album Echo Palace adds angular grooves and saxophone colour to the mix. A short move along the seafront takes you to Patterns’ basement.

name: Dove Ellis
bio: The Irish singer-songwriter pairs emotionally charged vocals with expansive, atmospheric songwriting. A more intimate thread in the middle of a guitar-heavy day, with space for delicate moments and soaring delivery.

name: Mike D 5D
bio: Mike D brings his 5D band to Mutations following the release of Thank You. The band includes his sons Skyler and Davis Diamond alongside Will Graefe, Eddie Ruscha and Milo Ruscha. Your longest set of the day anchors the evening at Chalk.

name: Painkiller
bio: The new project from Buzzard Buzzard Buzzard frontman Tom Rees. High-energy garage rock, plenty of fuzz and a punk streak kick off your late-night run at The Hope and Ruin.

name: Alien Chicks
bio: A Brixton trio who collide punk, rap and jazz with abrupt rhythmic shifts. Wiry riffs, rapid-fire delivery and intricate bass lines make for an unpredictable live set. No venue change needed: settle in for the second late-night chapter.

name: Cowboy Hunters
bio: Glasgow duo Megan Pollock and Desmond Johnston mix punk with huge beats and blunt humour. Releases such as Have A Pint and their EP EPeepee capture their rowdy, irreverent approach. The final stop on your route, after midnight on Sunday.
